events.title: Akinator closure contract frozen
events.hypothesis: A constant number of Akinator questions is not required; polynomial total dialogue is sufficient.
events.formal_statement: If deterministic exact SAT is decided with total cost <= N^c for one fixed c on every CNF, then SAT in P and therefore P=NP.
events.next_gap: Find a universally available exact question/observable family with polynomial total cost and certified progress.

events.title: Exact Walsh wave is not a free observable
events.hypothesis: Low-degree exact SAT-indicator wave coefficients might be cheap enough to guide the Akinator.
events.formal_statement: For G=F AND (NOT y) with fresh y, W_G({y})=#SAT(F); exact computation of even this degree-1 coefficient is #P-hard.
events.next_gap: Search for exact observables weaker than model counting.

events.title: Exact semantic split balance is #P-hard
events.hypothesis: The Akinator can cheaply choose a question that balances satisfying witnesses.
events.formal_statement: Exact balance needs #SAT(F AND q) and #SAT(F AND NOT q); these counts are #P-hard in general.
events.next_gap: Use proof-carrying structural progress rather than exact entropy/model balance.

events.title: Branch-or-answer trilemma frozen
events.formal_statement: Every exact question must yield certified collapse, keep both live branches, or pay for an exact semantic answer; heuristic discard is forbidden.
events.next_gap: Bound total branch mass or exact-answer cost.

events.title: Akinator mapped to SAT backdoor depth
events.formal_statement: Without a semantic oracle, adaptive variable questions form a backdoor-style decision tree; a supplied depth-d tree with polytime leaves costs O(2^d poly(N)).
events.external_basis: Dreier, Ordyniak, Szeider, SAT Backdoors: Depth Beats Size (2022).
events.next_gap: Prove shallow/poly-amortized depth or find counterfamilies.

events.title: BASE0 exact observable portfolio frozen
events.next_gap: Kill or prove each rung without silent heuristic fallback.

events.title: Expander graph-PHP selected as first BASE0/O5 stress family
events.reason: Root has no unit propagation; bounded-degree pigeon clauses are non-Horn/non-Krom; connected expanders defeat component decomposition; known Resolution width/size lower bounds attack O5.
events.next_gap: Determine whether repeated bounded-width contractions can evade the width lower bound under adaptive contexts.

events.title: Bounded-width contraction to Resolution-width bridge
events.hypothesis: Repeated bounded-width contractions under partial assignments might evade a Resolution width lower bound.
formal_statement: Root-global width-w contractions concatenate into one Resolution derivation of width <= max(w0(F),w).
If F|rho has a width-w residual derivation, pure Resolution lifts it to a subclause of D OR B(rho) with width <= max(w0(F),w+|rho|).
A complete O5(w) adaptive tree of branch depth d compiles to Resolution width <= max(w0(F),w+d).
The compiled Resolution DAG has size O(total local Resolution lines + branch-composition events).
external_basis: Ben-Sasson and Wigderson, Short Proofs are Narrow — Resolution Made Simple, ECCC TR99-022 / JACM 2001.
Their graph-PHP width theorem gives W(PHP(G)) >= r*e/2 for suitable bipartite expanders.
consequence: For bounded-degree expander graph-PHP, W=Omega(n), so fixed/logarithmic-width O5 requires branch depth Omega(n).
By Resolution size lower bounds and transcript-to-Resolution compilation, O5 total work is 2^{Omega(n)} in the literal-unit model, hence superpolynomial in encoded input length.
events.next_gap: Escalate beyond plain Resolution: identify the first stronger exact proof-carrying observable (likely B2/ER or another non-Resolution rule) that can contract graph-PHP while retaining polynomial discovery and total-cost bounds.

events.title: Independent O5 finite-mechanics replay passed
events.meaning: CI independently confirms the finite context-lift/branch-composition mechanics and validates JSON syntax. It does not establish the external asymptotic graph-PHP lower bound.
events.next_gap: Use graph-PHP as a separator to determine whether O7/B2/ER provides a constructive escape and locate the cost of generating the required extension definitions.

active_front.name: AKINATOR-CLOSE
active_front.current_exact_question: Can O7/B2/Extended Resolution construct a proof-carrying polynomial escape on the exact graph-PHP separator, and if so is the extension schema itself deterministically generable in polynomial time from the sparse input?
